newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius Telecom joins submarine cable project.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius Telecom joins submarine cable project.

text.p: State-owned Mauritius Telecom (MT) has joined a project aimed at laying a submarine optic fibre cable across the Indian Ocean to link Southern Africa and South East Asia via Mauritius by the year 2000.

A company official said on Friday: "Mauritius Telecom has signed a supplementary agreement to the SAFE (South Africa- Far East) Memorandum of Understanding signed between Telkom South Africa and Telekom Malaysia in July 1996, in South Africa."
The official added the memorandum opened the way to study the feasibility of the submarine cable project which expected to boost the use of Internet, telemedicine and video conferencing.

"The development process will include detailed studies of costs, routing configurations, technology and investment structures. This process will be completed by the end of this year at which time the parties will enter into a construction and maintenance agreement," the MT official said.
The three telecommunication companies did not exclude the possibility of other major international players joining the submarine cable project, the official added.
This would further extend the use of submarine cable communications systems between East Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas, the official said.
